correctness.rationale: In the periodic lift, consecutive centers cover their intervening positions exactly when the gap is at most 2r+1. At a center at 0 with predecessor/successor at −a,b, a private point must lie in [−r,r] intersected with [r−a+1,b−r−1]. The bounds on a,b make this intersection nonempty exactly when a+b≥2r+2; more distant centers cannot reach such a point. In the singleton case the copies of the same center do not overlap its closed interval since n≥2r+1; for k=2 the two neighbors can be distinct lifts of the same other center, as required. Rooting at a selected vertex gives exactly k roots per labeled set even for periodic gap words, yielding the n/k factor. The trace enumerates exactly these rooted words, and the formal logarithm and u derivative give 1/k and n respectively. The support inequalities are necessary by summation and sufficient by taking each gap in [r+1,2r+1]. At the upper endpoint n=k(r+1) every neighboring sum is tight, giving one constant word for odd k and 2r+1 alternating words for even k. The stated parity counts and examples follow. Independently replayed all subset-level gap conditions on 27 cases (r=1,2,3 and 2r+1≤n≤13) using private coverage multiplicities, and expanded the r=2 determinant by signed permutations; all matched.
residual_risks: The replay is bounded; the exact all-parameter result rests on the proof.
The Finding's awkward wording about nonzero coefficients is read as support equal to the stated interval, as explicitly proved in §4.

value.rationale: The result fills a natural refinement of cycle-power domination: it identifies every attainable size and gives exact multiplicities of irredundant covers rather than all covers. Extremal tightness yields explicit configurations and a parity distinction invisible in the upper domination number alone. This is useful structure throughout the natural family and not just a finite table.
residual_risks: No conclusion is drawn for nonuniform circular-arc systems or path powers.
